name: Dachepalli Publishers Limited
sector: K–12 educational publishing and school commerce
summary: Dachepalli has real catalogue and revenue expansion, but profits remain trapped in inventory and receivables. The gratuity/restatement bridge is explained; cash collection, connected-party support and new-commerce economics remain decisive. Conditional watch, not a demonstrated cash compounder. Full annual funding scenarios are supplied; IAS remains NS.

sections.title: Research Header and Scope
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026. Dachepalli Publishers Limited, INE1F9M01018, BSE SME code 544667, listed 30 December 2025; 14,976,000 shares and 1,200-share lot. Latest located dated secondary close is ₹97.25 on 16 October, not an official October 19 close. Analysis uses standalone audited March 2026 balances and a five-year horizon, 15 percent nominal pre-investor-tax analytical hurdle and ₹5 lakh reference position. G1–G4 are conditional, not automatic failure. [S1][S5][S6][S7][S14]

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: The company has an established curriculum catalogue and demonstrated growth, but has not demonstrated a cash-funded compounder. The IPO helped deleverage while large stocks, debtors and advances absorbed cash. Historical restatements and the FY 2026 gratuity catch-up are traceable, so an unexplained-comparative blanket hold is removed. Conditional watch is appropriate pending collection and operating-capital proof; neither the headline P/E nor a bullish sales projection is a purchase case. [S1][S2][S4]

sections.title: Scorecard and Gates
sections.text: BQS is 4.78; Growth Quality GQS is 5 after the persistent-CASH override, from raw 5.90. GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 5 and EARN 5 are supported. R is NS; D 2, P 4 and L 2 are conditional scores. IAS is NS, not a reweighted partial total. Low current-cash/model confidence does not erase the supported historical factors.

sections.title: Business Model
sections.text: Dachepalli develops and distributes school textbooks/curriculum content and bundled digital tools, with an in-house print process and outsourced author/vendor network. The prospectus lists 616 titles across brands and school boards, more than 75 authors, over 300 dealers and ten states/UTs, with a southern-India emphasis. New school commerce supplies stationery and other products; June 2026 adds interactive-board distribution. It is not simply a software platform or a government-backed subscription annuity. Manufacturing premises are leased from related School Book Company. [S1][S2][S8][S10]

sections.title: Competitive Position and Moat
sections.text: Catalogue familiarity, board alignment, teachers and dealer relationships provide useful advantages, but schools and distributors can switch. Digital tools support the print proposition; issuer-stated three-to-four-year retention is not an independently verified cohort. Author dependence, returns, syllabus updates and competitors limit pricing power. Top-ten distributor concentration rises from 17.15 percent FY 2023 to 42.07 percent FY 2025 andapproximately 45 percent H 1 FY 2026. The relevant peer archetype is a regional educational publisher with increasingly merchandise-heavy commerce, not high-margin pure software. No same-date peer-multiple dataset is claimed; exit multiples are transparent analytical assumptions. [S2]

sections.title: Demonstrated Revenue Growth
sections.text: FY 2023–FY 2026 operating revenues were ₹45.1948/50.8607/63.8992/91.3628 crore, giving predetermined three-year CAGR 26.44 percent and REV 8. Five comparable operating years were not established; original FY 2022 total income ₹25.2722 crore is separately identified, not silently mixed into revenue. New commerce is internally developed expansion, not acquired turnover. May management rounded FY 2026 sales to roughly ₹70 crore books and ₹20 crore commerce; no audited segment-margin split is available. Q 1 FY 2027 presentation sales ₹45.1785 crore more than double the comparator, but one quarter and a changed mix do not justify an extra score. [S1][S2][S3][S8][S11]

sections.title: Runway and Reinvestment Economics
sections.text: More schools, curriculum editions, digital bundles and commerce can expand reachable demand, but the constraint is funded inventory and collection, not a large generic education TAM. Management describes capacity that could support much higher revenue and limited near-term capex; this is not verified utilization or an economic-return guarantee. Reported core EBITDA₹23.4974 crore rises to an analytical ₹25.1413 crore after adding back the explicitly disclosed past-service gratuity catch-up. Incremental normalized accounting return is about 20.26 percent against a 12–15 percent assumed capital-cost range, but receivable-heavy profits and unknown commerce cohorts prevent a high CAP score. Forecast margins remain below that adjusted historical margin. [S1][S4][S8]

sections.title: Governance and Capital Allocation
sections.text: Family control and connected sales, purchases, premises and financing merit minority safeguards. FY 2026 sales to related Pelican Publishing House and School Book Company total ₹10.2712 crore, 11.24 percent of revenue; purchases from Dachepalli Printers total ₹2.9736 crore. Management describes ordinary-course arm-length terms; independent pricing evidence is unavailable. Interest-free related debt ₹24.9605 crore is supportive but remains repayable principal, not equity. The CARO loan-interest exception and adjacent no-new-loans statement need a borrower/amount reconciliation; neither proves diversion. No repayment default or disputed unpaid statutory dues are reported in the reviewed CARO period. [S1][S2][S5]

sections.title: Financial Quality and Cash Conversion
sections.text: FY 2023–FY 2026 reported CFO totals −₹13.9452 crore against positive profits, and −₹20.7820 crore after financing-classified interest. FY 2026 alone has CFO −₹22.8656 crore and cash capex ₹3.1574 crore; cash ends at ₹0.6663 crore despite ₹35.4857 crore net IPO cash. Receivables ₹74.5176 crore imply about 298 closing debtor days; inventory ₹54.53 crore implies about 292 days on average-inventory/COGS basis. Suppliers include ₹9.91 crore aged two to three years. School-year seasonality is plausible, but the July call’s expected later collections are not verified cash. Opening tax ₹5.8726 crore and noncurrent gratuity ₹1.8322 crore are explicitly treated once in the model. [S1][S2][S4]

sections.title: Historical and Forensic Review
sections.text: Prospectus restatement separately corrects past gratuity and deferred tax: full-note PAT FY 2023/FY 2024/FY 2025 is about ₹0.4747/3.3188/7.5624 crore versus original ₹0.8805/3.5662/8.3609 crore. FY 2026 annual note explicitly charges ₹1.6439197 crore past-service gratuity within ₹1.9545961 crore total benefit expense, explaining why its original comparative differs from the IPO-restated series. Small summary rounding differences are not a material reliability failure. FY 2025 original versus restated cash-flow classifications differ but both close at ₹3.6033 crore; FY 2026 cash rolls to ₹0.6663 crore. Issue costs ₹4.9063 crore exceed prospectus estimate ₹3.392 crore, reducing net proceeds by ₹1.5143 crore; CARO states funds were applied for their purposes, while the Reg 32 non-applicability notice does not give a full cumulative utilization bridge. No invented missing-cash allegation follows. [S1][S2][S9]

sections.title: Valuation and Funding Scenarios
sections.text: At the dated ₹97.25 close, market cap is ₹145.64 crore, about 9.58 times reported current-share FY 2026 profit. The annual model begins with actual operating WC₹110.8964 crore, cash ₹0.6663 crore and debt ₹35.0756 crore, separates interest-free family borrowing from bank debt, pays opening tax once and retains or settles the legacy gratuity claim explicitly. Base first-year/subsequent growth 35/20 percent, 23 percent margin, 105 percent WC/sales and 8× exit EBITDA imply ₹260.11 and 21.75 percent annual return, but peak year-end debt rises to ₹80.17 crore. Bear/bull prices are ₹48.00/₹707.92; severe losses can exhaust equity. Average-debt draw interest, supplier withdrawal, family recall, asset impairment, benefit timing, statutory-asset recovery and capex stresses are linked through cash and terminal equity. Current collections, opaque advances, commerce economics and support terms remain material low-confidence inputs; IAS is NS rather than a point value. [S1][S4][S8][S14]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A fivefold/tenfold price from ₹97.25 means ₹486.25/₹972.50 and 37.97/58.49 percent annual appreciation over five years. Linked reverse cases require about 46.23/72.21 percent constant revenue growth for 5×/10×, with peak year-end debt around ₹394.88/₹1088.74 crore under the same margin, capital intensity, tax and funding rules. These are algebraic requirements, not simply a higher P/E or a financeable forecast. Bull exceeds 5× only by combining sustained high growth, improved capital turnover and a higher exit multiple; financing requirements remain large. Classification: speculative feasibility, not demonstrated or probable multibagger. [S1][S4][S8]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Upgrade evidence would be a reconciled September/next reporting-date cash and receivable-aging bridge, actual realization of the July collection expectation, reduced return/obsolete-stock exposure, identifiable other advances, and a funded commerce-margin record. Track net debt including family loans, cash tax and benefit claims, aged suppliers, promoter/related transactions and issue proceeds. Deteriorating collections, supplier-credit withdrawal, related-loan recall or growth financed mainly by rising inventory would challenge even the base case. Verify current BSE quote/depth before any executable sizing. [S1][S4][S8][S14]

sections.title: Bear Case and What Would Change the View
sections.text: A strong bear case is that merchandise growth expands low-quality credit sales, textbook returns destroy inventory value and family support cannot be retained; the severe model links those losses to replacement financing. Counterevidence would be independently reconcilable collection after the school season, sustained gross margin after returns, low aged balances and funded repeat business. The disclosed restatement bridge is already counterevidence to an unexplained-profit allegation; it does not settle cash economics. The analysis would improve with cash evidence, not merely another guidance increase.

The corporate index was refreshed through 20 October; it is not proof that every exchange filing is captured. Official security metadata verifies BSE identity/lot; dated price and OHLCV are secondary and no BSE surveillance clearance is inferred. Remaining gaps are named in the audit rather than represented as completed facts.

GOV.reason: Family-connected sales, premises, procurement and interest-free funding require safeguards; historical benefit/tax corrections, the inconsistent loan-interest clause and incomplete proceeds-cost bridge limit control confidence. Known restatement is explained and is not evidence of intentional misstatement. No critical minority-abuse finding.

MOAT.reason: Curriculum catalogue, dealer/school relationships and bundled digital support provide useful but contestable distribution. Authors can leave, distributors sell competitors and premises are related-party leased; independently verified pricing power/retention is absent.

REV.reason: Predetermined three-year FY2023–26 operating-revenue CAGR 26.44 percent maps to 8. Five-year operating history is not established. Same-company new product commerce is organic expansion; it is not an acquisition or a net-agency-fee series. Lower-margin mix is addressed in earnings/capital quality, not by inventing missing organic growth. One strong quarter does not justify an upward trajectory adjustment.

DUR.reason: School demand, catalogue refresh and commerce cross-selling offer runway. Syllabus changes, digital alternatives, return rights, regional dependence and unverified per-school economics constrain durable excess-growth confidence.

CAP.reason: Reported/catch-up-adjusted accounting returns can exceed the 12–15 percent assumed capital-cost range, but large receivable/inventory growth and unproven commerce cohorts leave cash returns uncertain. No high-return reinvestment score is awarded from accounting ROE alone.

CASH.reason: Four-year cumulative operating cash is negative despite profits and remains weaker after financing-classified interest. FY2025 conversion was already weak, while FY2026 adds major inventory/debtors and aged supplier credit. Seasonal explanations require subsequent evidence; this is not merely subtracting capex from CFO.

BAL.reason: IPO reduced debt and interest-free family support lowers current finance cost, but only 0.6663 crore cash remains, material tax must settle and growth requires new working-capital funds. Related principal remains a liability; recall or weak collections can force market refinancing.

EXEC.reason: Revenue/catalogue and new commerce scale are demonstrated, but collection, issue-cost and funding discipline lag. Management projections and product announcements are not credited as completed cash returns.

EARN.reason: Operating profits rise beyond other income and lower interest; the disclosed past-service catch-up depresses rather than inflates current earnings. New-commerce mix, returns and repeated cash-investment demands limit confidence in margin persistence. Current-share earnings are used, not an IPO weighted-share boost.

R.reason: The base 21.75 percent model return is conditional on a large unverified collection improvement, unclear other-advance recovery, commerce margins and continued low-cost related support. These material inputs do not support a point prospective-return score; lack of scenario probabilities alone is not the reason.

D.reason: The linked severe case can exhaust equity through receivable/inventory losses, supplier-credit withdrawal and family-loan refinancing. Leased premises and cash-poor working assets do not establish a reliable hard-asset recovery floor.

P.reason: A roughly 9.6 times current-share reported P/E is not expensive on headline earnings, but price support depends on converting profits into cash. The base needs sustained growth/margin and financing, while severe recovery fails; a low P/E alone is insufficient protection.

L.reason: Observed 60-row low×volume median implies 10.57 days at 5 percent, starting band 3. Downgraded one point for a23.34 percent reference-position lot, stale secondary quote, missing-session uncertainty and absent live depth. No automatic trading suspension or zero-volume assumption.

gates.reason: Related transactions and control/disclosure questions require safeguards; no substantiated critical minority-abuse finding.
Known restatement/catch-up and cash reclassifications are explained. Opaque advances and subsequent cash realization remain specific uncertainties, not a blanket reporting failure.
Family support and IPO deleveraging help, but actual cash is low and tax, commerce growth and collection stress require substantial uncommitted funding.
Secondary dated quote, 23.34 percent reference-position lot and incomplete session/depth evidence constrain execution; no unsupported suspension claim.

valuation.status: Conditional linked annual operating, funding and terminal-equity scenarios; not a point valuation
valuation.units: INR crore except shares and INR per share
valuation.opening_WC_formula: 74.5176 receivables + 54.5300 inventory + 7.7302 other advances + 1.2707 operating security deposits - 26.1388 trade payables - 0.7786 statutory payables - 0.2347 current non-tax provisions = 110.8964. Noncurrent gratuity 1.8322 is excluded and explicitly retained/settled separately.
methodology: Actual March 2026 audited balances anchor opening claims. IPO cash is already in opening equity/cash and is not raised again. Current 14,976,000 shares are retained; no assumed rescue equity or market sales change issuer cash.

FY2026 reported EBITDA excluding other income is 23.4974 crore. The annual note identifies 1.6439197 crore past-service gratuity catch-up within current expense, giving a conditional recurring EBITDA bridge of 25.1413197 crore before any other normalization. Forecast margins of 18/23/25 percent are independent, explicitly lower analytical assumptions, not a blind extrapolation of this catch-up adjustment or unaudited segment margins.

Publishing and new school commerce have different margins and working capital. The report does not supply audited segment EBITDA/capital; the model uses whole-company revenue/margins rather than inventing segment accounts. FY2027 growth 10/35/60 percent and subsequent 5/20/30 percent are scenario assumptions. The separately tested 150 crore management revenue guidance is not the base forecast.

Actual opening WC excludes the 1.6148 crore ambiguously described statutory asset. No automatic tax offset is assumed; a separate recovery case tests its receipt once without adding revenue. Bank deposit 0.194 is not opening spendable cash and has conditional terminal recovery.

Opening current income tax 5.8726 crore is paid once in FY2027, separately from 28 percent positive-profit cash tax. Existing statutory dues and current non-tax provisions are already deducted within WC; detailed current gratuity 0.1224 plus CSR 0.1124 differ by 0.0001 crore rounding from the 0.2347 balance-sheet residual and must not be paid again. The deferred-tax liability is not an immediate cash tax demand; forecast cash tax is an explicit simplified assumption.

Noncurrent gratuity 1.8322 crore is outside operating WC and retained as a terminal equity deduction in core scenarios. FY2027 and FY2029 settlement sensitivities pay it once and remove the terminal deduction. Recurring compensation is included and cash-paid in forecast margins and does not extinguish the separate opening benefit claim.

Interest-free related-party loans 24.9605 crore are retained as debt, not equity. Core base does not fabricate a repayment demand or perpetually waive the principal; terminal equity deducts it in full. Recall sensitivities repay half/all in FY2027 and require market replacement funding, while an alternative prices retained related loans at 10 percent. Actual recall/support commitments are unverified.

Interest-bearing opening debt 10.1151 crore includes current maturities 1.6491. That first-year principal is paid once; 1.5 crore later annual amortization is illustrative, not the exact mixed-loan calendar. Interest uses average opening/closing term, related and new WC debt with circular draw/tax calculation. Funding required is not sanctioned capacity.

The 9.91 crore supplier balance aged two to three years is already deducted in opening WC. A withdrawal stress increases the future WC level by 9.91 once relative to the same operating ratio; it is not an additional duplicate payment of opening trade payables. No verified supplier recall is alleged.

Debtor/inventory impairment reduces usable opening WC, enters PAT as a noncash loss and is added back in CFO; replacement funding enters delta WC once. No tax shield on impairment is assumed. Returns/obsolete textbooks and merchandise collection risk are not presumed fully provided.

Maintenance/ordinary growth capex is 2.5 percent of sales; separate 10 crore expansion sensitivity has no invented incremental profit. Existing equipment is not purchased again. FY2031 terminal EBITDA multiples exclude a second addition of operating inventory/receivables/PPE. No probability-weighted forecast or guaranteed liquidity is asserted.
